# Attention Is All You Need

## 1 Introduction

Recurrent models compute hidden states sequentially, which precludes parallelization within a training example. ^s1p1

## 3.2.1 Scaled Dot-Product Attention

We compute the dot products of the query with all keys, divide each by $\sqrt{d_k}$, and apply a softmax function to obtain the weights on the values. ^s3p1

For large values of $d_k$, the dot products grow large in magnitude, pushing the softmax function into regions where it has extremely small gradients. ^s3p2

# Scaled dot-product attention
#chapter [status:: unread]

## In one sentence

Every query scores every key by a dot product, the scores are shrunk by $\sqrt{d_k}$ so the softmax stays soft, and the weights mix the values.

## From the paper

![[papers/vaswani-2017/source#^s3p1]]

![[papers/vaswani-2017/source#^s3p2]]

## Notation

| symbol | meaning |
|---|---|
| $d_k$ | the width of a query or key vector |

## Where it stops holding

The $\sqrt{d_k}$ argument assumes the components of $q$ and $k$ are independent with unit variance; with a learned scale the constant matters less.

## Question

What happens to the gradient of the softmax when $d_k$ grows and the scores are not scaled?
